D_offset = 0 taken at the ridge-R minimum, which falls at geometric D = +0.006 V/nm — i.e. the gap minimum locates D = 0 where the geometry puts it; stated, not assumed.

Si (contact-doping gate, ±25 V available) is the knob that could push it away …

**Raw:** R(B) is a low-density trace — broad non-sinusoidal features (peak 330 Ω at 2.45 T, near-zero minima at 1.7 and 2.05 T), then the fully symmetry-broken integer-QH ladder above ~5 T (minima at 5.0, 6.0, 6.95, 8.3 T), R → 590 Ω at 10 T. **FFT [1, 5] T (δF 1.25 T, only 4–6 periods):** one broad peak at 7.5 T with low-frequency weight at 2.5–4.4 T (scratch windows resolve ~4.4 and 6.8 and a weak 12.3). **Read:** the content sits at and below F_L × 0.886 = 11.0 T — 4.4 + 6.8 ≈ 11.2 would be a close, balanced pair summing to the full density (the ABAB near-CNP semimetal template; model at n_true = −1.06: 4.4 / 5.9 T), but the record cannot separate the two tones cleanly; an ABCA hole pocket here (m* ≈ 1 mₑ) would be LK-dead at T_e ≈ 8 K, so its absence is not evidence. **Weight: consistent-with ABAB, uninformative against ABCA** (resolution- and temperature-limited, as priced). **Lever-arm by-product:** the integer-ladder 1/B spacings above 4.5 T (0.0215–0.025 T⁻¹ per filling step, one 1.5-step outlier) give n·h/e ≈ 40–46 T → n = 0.97–1.1×10¹² at this gate point vs n_cal = 1.20 — an independent density scale of **0.80–0.92**, bracketing the electron-side Luttinger scale 0.886 from run 6. [ana cell 23] # THE CALL — <device> stacking (tetralayer-stacking-fs-count, Step 7)

## 1. Per-region verdict

- **Channel B_1−B_2 (the only wired 4T pair; probes regions A + B in series): ABAB (Bernal) — strong.**
- Region B separately (the faint parallel CNP ridge, +0.43×10¹² electron-doped vs A): **uninformative on its own** — no tone set attributable solely to B was resolved (expected B-region tones at ×1.13 the A-frequencies fall within δF of the A set at low weight); its presence does not perturb the A read.
- No other regions are addressable this cooldown (T_1–T_4 dead, hardwired configuration).

## 2. Evidence (all runs this session; per-tone coordinates at n_cal = +3.2×10¹², D = 0 unless stated)

1. **Pair partitioning F_L** — tones **7.3 T** and **22.0 T** (run 6, FFT [1, 5.5] T, δF 1.2), sum 29.3 T = F_L(g = 4) at one global scale **0.886** (partition 0.25 / 0.75; ABAB model 0.23 / 0.77 at this n). Luttinger check: closes at scale 1 of the calibrated density × 0.886.
2. **Onsager overlay across density** (run 8 fan, 61 columns, n_cal 1.6–3.25×10¹²): both branches track the **ABAB F(n)** curves under the single scale; sum = F_L(n) column-by-column; dual overlay vs trilayer ML+BL fails by trajectory (adjacent-N check passed — the transport supports N = 4).
3. **F_L-tone origin (mandatory discrimination): combination/breakdown, not a pocket** — (a) a **difference tone** f_heavy − f_light appears at every fan column with a non-Onsager (n-flat) trajectory; (b) B-window split: sum/heavy amplitude 0.55 → 1.03, diff/light 0.27 → 1.6 with rising B (run 6); (c) LK mass of the F_L tone 0.051–0.069 mₑ ≥ heavy branch, toward m_l + m_h.
4. **LK mass split** (runs 9–14, rungs 1.2–30 K): light 0.028 ± 0.002 mₑ (= ABAB model), heavy 0.041–0.057 (window fork; model 0.061), 2×light harmonic confirmed by mass; beat exclusion decisive (light < heavy).
5. **Degeneracy audit:** g = 4 scale 0.886 independently confirmed by the hole-side symmetry-broken integer ladder (run 7: scale 0.80–0.92) and the fan's QH minima spacing (0.87–0.88 at 8–10 T) — no flavor polarization at the operating point.
6. Hole side (run 7, n_cal = −1.2×10¹²): content at/below F_L×0.886 consistent with the ABAB near-CNP balanced pair; **consistent-with** only (4–6 periods, δF ≈ 1.2 on 4–7 T tones).

## 3. Confidence and hedges

- **Strong, not decisive**: the heavy-branch mass is extraction-window dependent (0.038–0.057; the [3.5, 7] T window cannot separate heavy from sum, δF = 7 T) — the φ² mass-ratio check re…

[ana cell 29] **Read: one Fermi pocket.** Four of the five densities return **exactly one** unflagged SdH
tone; the fifth (n = +1.99) has all its tones flagged marginal or harmonic and yields none.
**No density yields two.** The two highest-contrast traces — n = +0.99 and +1.49 × 10¹² cm⁻²,
contrast 19.4 and 8.3 — give f/f_full = **0.835** and **0.834**, and a fit through the
origin over |n| > 0.9 gives 8.62 T per 10¹² cm⁻² against the 10.34 full-Onsager slope.

**That is the discriminating fact, and it needs no calibration.** Two Fermi pockets would
put the dominant tone near 0.7× the full Onsager value *and* add a second tone near 0.3×,
both scaling linearly with n. Neither appears. A Bernal (ABAB) tetralayer at D = 0 has two
bilayer-like bands with different masses, both crossing E_F at any finite density, and would
show exactly that two-tone structure. A rhombohedral (ABCA) stack has a single quartic band
and shows what we see.

**An independent consistency check falls out.** Reading the 0.834 ratio as a single 4-fold
degenerate pocket gives α = 1.199 for the absolute density scale. The Landau fan's minima
ladder — a completely different observable, from run 4 — gave α = 1.166. **The two agree to
2.8 %.** That does not break the α/g degeneracy (both routes still measure only the product),
but it does say the two datasets are describing the same Fermi surface consistently.

**Caveats.** The two low-|n| traces are unreliable and I am not using them in the fit:
n = +0.49 and −0.81 carry too few oscillations over the field range, and their apparent
ratios (1.02, 1.36) scatter accordingly. The hole side reaches only −0.81 × 10¹² cm⁻²
because the top-gate limit bounds it, so the pocket count is really established on the
electron side. And a *second* pocket much smaller than the first — carrying, say, under 10 %
of the carriers — would produce a tone below 1.5 T that the degree-5 background removal
would eat; this measurement excludes two comparable pockets, not a small satellite.

much stronger check than any single column, and it is what would expose a spurious peak.

stays modest; the n = +0.50 column sits at ν ≈ 3.4 at 6 T and may clip near its

SdH *minima* — run 4 showed those reaching 0–6 Ω, and the minima are half the signal.

but it does say the two datasets are describing the same Fermi surface consistently.

[ana cell 33] **Read: a displacement-field-driven metal–insulator crossover at charge neutrality, and a
gap that is real but small.**

At D ≈ 0 the neutrality point is **metallic** — Δ = **−0.62 ± 0.17 meV**, i.e. R_CNP *rises*
with temperature (249 Ω at 1.2 K → 360 Ω at 40 K). By D/ε₀ = +0.238 V/nm it is **insulating**
— Δ = **+1.36 ± 0.14 meV**, R_CNP falling 2975 Ω → 1175 Ω over the same range. The sign of
dR/dT flips at **D = +0.126 V/nm**, and all seven isotherms cross at that single point. The
+D flank rises at 7.9 meV per V/nm.

**This is the cleanest exclusion of ABAB in the session.** A Bernal tetralayer is a
band-overlapped semimetal: displacement field gaps each bilayer-like subband but shifts them
relative to one another, so the overlap survives and neutrality stays metallic at all D.
A metal→insulator crossover driven purely by D is not that.

**The inversion-symmetry test, done properly.** Δ(D) is plainly curved near its minimum, so
extrapolating a straight line from the +D flank back to zero — which an earlier version of
this cell did, returning a meaningless −1.12 meV intercept — is the wrong statistic. The right
one is *where the minimum sits*. A parabola over the 29 points around it gives
**D = +0.016 ± 0.004 V/nm**, against run 3's independent R_CNP minimum at
**0.000 ± 0.008 V/nm**. Both sit within ~4 % of the accessible D range of zero.

**But the magnitude does not behave like a clean band gap, and that is the honest limit
here.** 1.36 meV at D ≈ 0.25 V/nm is one to two orders of magnitude below what a rhombohedral
tetralayer's single-particle gap should be at that field. Together with R_CNP's saturation
near 3 kΩ (run 3), this says the transport is **disorder- and parallel-channel-limited**:
in-gap states and a shunt path put a floor under the resistance long before the true gap
would. That is entirely ordinary for gapped graphene multilayers — measured activation
energies routinely run 10–30× below the band gap — but it means this measurement establishes
the gap's **existence and D-dependence**, not its size. Any claim of the form "the gap is
X meV" is not supported; "a gap opens with |D| and closes near D = 0" is.

The base-temperature point is excluded from every fit: R_CNP is flat between 1.2 and 8 K,
exactly as the rig's ~8 K electron temperature predicts, so those points carry no independent
information.

[measure cell 46] … *resistance*. This says it in **meV**.

**Why this is the measurement that closes the argument.** Run 3's R_CNP(D) has one feature
that does not look like a cleanly growing single-particle gap: above D/ε₀ ≈ 0.23 V/nm it
**saturates** near 3 kΩ instead of continuing up exponentially. That is the signature of a
parallel conduction path or disorder-induced in-gap states putting a floor under the
resistance — and if that floor dominates, "R rose 10×" would be a weaker claim than it
looks. Thermal activation settles it: fitting R_CNP(T) ∝ exp(Δ/2k_BT) at each D returns a
gap in meV whose *D-dependence* is the physics. ABCA requires Δ(D) growing with |D| and
extrapolating to ≈ 0 at D = 0; ABCB requires a finite Δ at D = 0.

**It is also the one measurement immune to the unknown geometry.** The device card gives no
Hall-bar dimensions, so every resistance this session is in ohms, not ohms-per-square, and
the geometric prefactor is unknown. Activation is a *ratio* measurement — the prefactor
cancels exactly. So does the ~7–10 % probe-loading systematic, provided it does not itself
depend on temperature.

**Design.** At each temperature, one 245-point co-swept `multisweep` that walks the
session-measured CNP line (`V_bg = −1.2737·V_tg − 0.00764`) five times at perpendicular
V_bg offsets of 0, ±0.05, ±0.10 V, folded into a single path and reshaped to (5, 49) in
analysis. The offsets matter: they let R_CNP be taken as the **maximum over offsets** at
each point along the line, so a few-mV drift in the fitted line — or thermal drift of the
CNP itself as the sample warms — cannot masquerade as a change in gap. One sweep covers
D/ε₀ = −0.094 → +0.285 V/nm, so every temperature yields a complete R_CNP(D) curve in
under 4 minutes.

**Temperatures:** base, then 8, 12, 17, 23, 30, 40 K via `set_both(T, ratio=0.95)` — the
rig-card-sanctioned ratio; any deviation is consent-gated and is not used. Points are
accepted on **stability, not proximity**: the rig card records that the sample loop is
untuned, overshoots ~+1.4 K, and recovers only as fast as the bath allows, so waiting for
|T − setpoint| to close never converges below ~20 K. `T_sample` is followed per point, so
the Arrhenius fit uses the temperature actually measured, never the setpoint. The ladder
starts at 8 K deliberately — the rig's electron temperature is ~8 K, so nothing below that
carries independent information.

**Field to zero first.** Activation must be measured at B = 0 or a Landau gap contaminates
Δ. The …

[ana cell 22] ## Run 4 — `landau-fan`: band structure at D = 0, and a correction

**Why / what we're testing:** the gate map settled the call on gap physics. This is an
independent look at the *band structure* — 40 field rows (0.75 → 6 T, uniform in 1/B) ×
46 densities co-swept along the session-measured D = 0 line, n = −1.05 → +2.09 × 10¹² cm⁻²
with the CNP at V_tg = −0.003.

**Correction to the proposing cell.** When I launched this run I claimed the Landau-level
degeneracy would separate ABCA from ABAB — that a rhombohedral tetralayer's 4-fold orbital
zero level (16 states, first gaps at ν = ±8) would look different from a Bernal one.
**That is wrong, and I retract it.** ABAB tetralayer decomposes into two effective bilayers,
each carrying a 2-fold orbital zero level × 4 spin/valley = 8 states, and both sit at
exactly E = 0 — so ABAB also has 16 zero-energy states. The zero-LL degeneracy is 4N for
N layers *regardless of stacking*: it counts **layers, not stacking order**. The measure
notebook is append-only so the original claim stands there; this is the corrected record.

What this run can still do is count **Fermi pockets**, which does discriminate: a
rhombohedral stack has one quartic band at D = 0, a Bernal tetralayer has two bilayer-like
bands both crossing E_F and therefore two SdH tones.

> **12:20** · bg-cut: sr1 sens 2uV->1mV + sr0/sr1 tau 0.3->0.1 s (operator-authorized), then 1D V\_bg +2.00 to -1.30 V, 133 pts @ 25 mV, V\_tg=0, V\_si=0, B=0, T=base, delay 0.7 s (7 tau) · **ETA ~12:24** (≈4 min)

Plan step **P1** (second pass). Run 0 passed Gate C but clipped the one channel that
matters. This cell fixes the acquisition and repeats the cut; it costs ~2.5 min and
gates the ~45 min map that follows, so it runs first.

**What run 0 established.** The drain current traces a clean, symmetric dip centred at
**V_bg = −0.200 V** at V_tg = 0 — that is the CNP, and on the geometry prior it puts the
intrinsic doping at n_offset ≈ +3.0 × 10¹¹ cm⁻² (slightly electron-doped) with the CNP
sitting at D/ε₀ ≈ +0.027 V/nm, i.e. essentially zero field. Leakage is clean: both gate
currents are flat and voltage-independent (TG −100 pA, BG +25 pA offsets), and the ~100 pA
spikes appear **simultaneously on both independent gates**, which is pickup or a read
collision, not leakage — real gate leakage cannot be common-mode across two separate
Keithleys.

**Why sr1 must be re-ranged.** Rxx clipped at 218 Ω (fs 1.09) over 30 % of the sweep,
so the CNP peak height is unmeasured. The drain current cannot substitute: the 100 MΩ
bias resistor defines the current, so a device going 100 Ω → 100 kΩ moves I by ~0.1 %.
New sensitivity **1 mV** = 100 kΩ of Rxx headroom at 10 nA bias, which covers a flat-band
CNP; the metallic end (65 Ω, 0.65 µV) sits 60 dB down, well inside an SR830's reserve.

**Why τ drops to 0.1 s.** Compliant dwell is 7τ, so 0.3 s costs 2.1 s/pt and prices the
coarse map at ~1.9 h; 0.1 s costs 0.7 s/pt and prices it at ~45 min. At the 13.777 Hz
drive a 100 ms 24 dB/oct filter still puts 2f (27.6 Hz) about 99 dB down. It is set on
**sr0 as well as sr1** — the dwell is gated by the slowest channel, so re-ranging only
sr1 would buy nothing. Both are instrument-configuration writes on lock-in inputs; no
validator, gate limit, field cap or T cap is touched.

input is 10 MΩ: ~0.8 MΩ of series probe resistance divides Vxx down by ~7 %, and worse
if the probe contacts go strongly resistive at the CNP. So absolute Rxx carries a
